title: [recoverability] The Rust readers that compare a stored commit id with git read it through the commit map: the controller's commit against the owner's landing (the integrator's wait and the controller_behind alert), spawn mission moved --from/--to, and the restore drill's recorded heads against live; a dropped id says so, and an id in neither the map nor the source is an unknown commit, never behind, does-not-descend or mismatch
prompt:
Spawn, objective 178 [recoverability] (projects-47, 2026-11-14: the history-rewrite line, sites 8/9, 16 and 17 of rev-b's survey; rev-e; reviewer rev-f): the Rust readers that compare a stored commit id with git read it through the commit map (objective 173). It lands with 177 before the rewrite.

Why. The owner rewrites the Spawn repository's history tonight. Every changed commit gets a new id, an empty one is dropped, and the old objects are pruned. 173 loads git filter-repo's map (`spawn commit-map load`, spawn_commit_map) and reads the integrator's SQL through spawn_commit_now. Three Rust readers still compare an id recorded before the rewrite with git as it is now:
- Site 8/9, the controller's commit. deploy/controller.sh names a controller directory controllers/<name>-<40 hex> after the commit it was built from. controller_behind (integrate.rs) and the controller_behind alert (alerts.rs read_controllers) ask git whether that commit is an ancestor of the owner's latest landing (already translated in SQL by 173). After the rewrite the old id is no commit of the source. merge-base fails, so the task never waits for the deploy and is judged with the old controller's scenarios (P22, task 259's failure), and the alert never fires.
- Site 16, `spawn mission moved --from/--to` (missions.rs). deploy.sh records a deploy from the live controller's commit, or from a pending file written before the rewrite. The old --from is refused as "does not descend" and the deploy dies.
- Site 17, the restore drill's recorded heads against live (backup/restore_drill.rs). A bundle made before the rewrite records the old head ids. Each one compares as "restored at <old>; live is at <new>, which does not descend from it": a mismatch, so the drill fails every resource for a day.

What changes (the candidate, 178-fleet.diff, no protected path):
- crates/spawn-cli/src/commit_now.rs (new). CommitNow::of(commit, entry, held) reads one recorded id: the map's new id when the map holds it (Commit(new)); Dropped when the map names no new commit; else the id itself when the repository holds it as a commit; else Unknown. commit_now(store, repository, commit) does the same with store.commit_map_entry and `git -C <repository> cat-file -e <id>^{commit}` (read only, controller_git, nothing that begins with '-'). id_or_why(what, commit) gives the id, or rev-b's words: "<what> <id> was dropped by the history rewrite (the commit map names no new commit for it)" / "<what> <id> is an unknown commit (in neither the commit map nor the source)".
- integrate.rs, site 8/9:
  - controller_behind(repository, scenarios, landed, now) returns ControllerLag::{No, Behind(new id), Unknown(why)}. It reads the controller's commit through `now` before the ancestry check. A store error is an error, not a verdict.
  - The integrator's wait: Behind waits as before. Unknown is said once per task (Wait::ControllerUnknown) and is never a wait: the task is judged, exactly as when merge-base failed before.
- alerts.rs read_controllers, site 8/9: the same function with the map. Unknown is never behind. A store error is said like the reading's other errors.
- missions.rs `mission moved`, site 16: --from and --to are each read through the map. The new ids are compared and recorded (source.moved from m1' to X). A dropped or unknown one is refused with its words, never "does not descend".
- backup/restore_drill.rs, site 17:
  - compare_refs reads each restored head through the map, then live. Mapped to live's commit is "the same"; one that live moved past is "moved on since"; only an id that live holds can be a mismatch.
  - A dropped head is listed in Refs.dropped, said on its own line and counted on the source's line. It is not a failure: the rewrite removed an empty commit and nothing of it is lost.
  - A head in neither the map nor live is listed in Refs.unknown. It fails the drill (exit 1) as "unknown commit", never "mismatch": "restore-drill: unknown commit: …" and "FAILED: N mismatch(es) and M unknown commit(s) older than bundle …".
  - The record's shape is unchanged: its `mismatches` count is both, and its reason says both.
  - The source's line is unchanged unless a dropped or unknown head exists; then it gains ", D dropped by the history rewrite, U unknown commit(s)". So deploy/backup/test-restore-drill.sh's greps hold.
  - restore_repo still verifies the bundle against its own recorded old ids and objects: nothing old is substituted.

The lead chose these behaviours (projects-47, 2026-11-14): a dropped drill head is named but does not fail; an unknown one fails as "unknown commit" inside mismatches; a dropped or unknown controller is said once and is not a wait.

What stays as it is: the schema and 173's API, the record shapes, the event log (old ids stay), every SQL reader, and the drill's verification of the bundle itself.

Tests:
- commit_now unit tests: a mapped id is its new one without asking the repository; a dropped id is Dropped even when the repository still holds it; an unmapped id is itself when held, else Unknown; the two sentences word for word.
- integrate::tests:
  - a_main_ahead_of_its_controller_is_a_descendant_of_its_commit (kept, on the new signature). With no map, a commit the repository lacks is now ControllerLag::Unknown with its sentence (before: None).
  - a_controller_built_before_the_rewrite_is_compared_by_its_new_commit: an old id mapped to new1 is behind new2 and not behind new1; dropped is Unknown with the dropped sentence; a store error is an error.
- integrate::database_tests, through the real store and spawn_commit_map:
  - a_controller_from_before_the_rewrite_holds_the_task_through_the_map: the controller spawn-<old>, map old -> m0, the owner lands past m0. The task waits (Wait::Controller) and no gate starts. With the controller switched to a dropped commit, the task is judged and accepted.
  - the_controller_behind_alert_reads_the_controller_through_the_map: the loop's Monitor fires controller_behind after the bound, with evidence.controller = m0 (the new id) and landed = the owner's commit. Switched to a dropped controller, it clears.
- backup::restore_drill::tests:
  - refs_compare_allowing_descendants_and_refs_made_or_removed_since (kept, identity map).
  - restored_heads_are_compared_with_live_through_the_commit_map: same, newer, dropped, unknown and a mapped mismatch ("restored at o2 (now n3)"), the line's suffix, outcome() counting the unknown without calling it a mismatch, and a store error.
- The alert path is reached only by the loop's monitor (commands/loops.rs), which no scenario runs (P22's own alert has none either). Its mutant is killed through the store, by the database test.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/commit_now.rs (new), spawn-cli/src/{main,integrate,alerts,missions}.rs, spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs, spawn-cli/src/integrate/{tests,database_tests}.rs. Owner: rsi/scenarios/178.sh. Size: +709 −72 in one crate. About 330 of that is code and doc comments; the rest is tests. It touches none of 177's files except integrate.rs, integrate/tests.rs and integrate/database_tests.rs, and `git merge-tree` of 177 (76d6e7dd) and 178 merges with no conflict.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/178.sh, black box. It has its own database, scratch HOME and GNUPGHOME, and a local R2 stand-in (104's). The world is one gated mission whose gate is a controller directory (deploy/controller.sh's layout).
- Before the rewrite: the owner lands m1 and the controller is deployed at m1. `spawn backup bundle` records main at m1, `e` at an empty E on m1, and `lost` at L on m1.
- The rewrite: m0 is kept and m1 becomes m1'. E is dropped and `e` moves to m1'. L is unmapped and `lost` moves to m1'. Every old object is pruned (gc --prune=now), and the map is loaded.
- After it: the owner lands X on m1', and a reported task waits for its gate.
(1) One `spawn integrate --once`: the controller spawn-<m1> is behind X through the map. No gate runs, the task has no verdict, and the integrator says it waits for the deploy.
(2) Controller switched to spawn-<E>: the next pass judges the task. The integrator says "the controller's commit <E> was dropped by the history rewrite (the commit map names no new commit for it)" and never says it is behind.
(3) `spawn mission moved --from <m1> --to <X>` exits 0 and records source.moved {from: m1', to: X}.
(4) --from <E> is refused with "--from <E> was dropped by the history rewrite (…)". --from <40 ones> is refused with "--from <id> is an unknown commit (in neither the commit map nor the source)". Neither says "does not descend".
(5) `spawn backup restore-drill`: "0 the same, 1 moved on since (descendants), … 0 mismatch(es), 1 dropped by the history rewrite, 1 unknown commit(s)". e is said dropped and lost is said an unknown commit; no line calls any head a mismatch. The drill exits 1 with "FAILED: 0 mismatch(es) and 1 unknown commit(s)", and backup.drilled.missions is {ok: false, mismatches: 1}.
The base (173, e36a0ea3) exits 1 with 17 failed checks: at (1) the gate runs; at (2) nothing is said; at (3) and (4) "Not a valid commit name" / "does not descend"; at (5) three mismatches.

Proof: 178-proof.txt (rev-e).

Verified by: tonight's rewrite. After MAP LIVE, the controller deployed before the rewrite (controllers/spawn-<old id>) holds a task while an owner's landing is undeployed, and the deploy's `spawn mission moved --from <old>` records from the new id. The next daily drill on the pre-rewrite bundle passes, or names only unknown commits, with no "mismatch" for a mapped head.
